name: pediatric ataxia overview
title: A child with ataxia: localize it (hemisphere for limb ataxia, vermis for truncal ataxia), then sort the three most common causes (intoxication, acute postinfectious cerebellar ataxia, brain tumour) from the can't-miss causes (stroke or hemorrhage, meningitis or encephalitis, brain tumour) by the history, then a shared exam step (how to examine a child under 5) leads to whether to image and what to do; hereditary Friedreich ataxia, slowly progressive with absent reflexes, has its own column

root.title: Child with ataxia: a SIGN, not a diagnosis
lines: cerebellum: trouble walking or sitting, falls to one side, slurred speech, low tone, intention tremor
cerebellar HEMISPHERE → limbs: over- or undershoots, clumsy · VERMIS → trunk: can't sit, wide-based gait
also from vestibular disease (severe vertigo, vomiting, positional) or weakness, sensory or position-sense loss
by stage: not walking → can't sit unsupported, misreaches · walking → wide-based, unsteady, clumsy, dysmetria, intention tremor
IMAGE (MRI preferred, CT more accessible) if: ANY other neurologic finding · SUBACUTE course (weeks to months) · TRAUMA

groups.title: CAN'T MISS: rule in or out every time

head: h
Intoxication
any sedative-hypnotic
pres: • abuse red flags: bruises, changing story
somnolent · sibling's carbamazepine within reach → poison control
inv: if not very altered and can be watched in the emergency department
case: 4, empty dextromethorphan bottle → no imaging

head: h
Acute postinfectious cerebellar ataxia
direct viral infection or autoimmune
pres: • varicella, mono, respiratory or gut virus
• ABRUPT, worse over 1-2 days, better over weeks
afebrile, well · daycare viruses within a month · wide-based gait
inv: a recent virus does not confirm it

head: h
Brain tumour
medulloblastoma · cerebellar astrocytoma
pres: • invades cerebellum or blocks CSF → hydrocephalus
after a virus · headaches (family migraine) · marked LEFT dysmetria → medulloblastoma
inv: case: 6, clumsy + headaches 3 months, dysmetria only

head: h
Stroke · hemorrhage · infarction
cerebellar vessel blocked or bleeding
pres: • trigger: chiropractic neck adjustment (dissection), car crash
inv: case: 3, unsteady after a chiropractor that afternoon

head: h
Meningitis · encephalitis
viral or bacterial
inv: case: 7, fever 4 days, vomiting, overshoots, stiff neck

rows: • reach for a favourite toy or food, each hand
• follow a toy across the visual field
• poke a foot while distracted: does the child look?
• toddlers are wide-based anyway: ask if it is NEW
